subtitle: The Five Brothers of Ma'abar and the Tooth of the Buddha

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of Kulasekara on a sea cliff, ships behind him
panels.action: Maravarman Kulasekara Pandyan I stands in royal armor on a rocky Tamil shore at sunset, waves crashing around him and distant ships headed towards Sri Lanka silhouetted on the horizon.

dialogue.text: In Kulasekara’s age, five Pandyan brothers ruled pearl-bright Ma'abar—until one sailed to Sri Lanka, seized the Buddha’s Tooth, and then chose to send it back.

i18n.hi: कुलसेकर के समय में मोती जैसा चमकता माबर पाँच पांड्य भाइयों के हाथ में था—तब एक भाई श्रीलंका गया, बुद्ध का दाँत उठा लाया, फिर खुद ही उसे लौटाने का फैसला किया।

panels.shot: slow push-in from bustling port to Kulasekara in court
panels.action: A sweeping scene of the Ma'abar coast: Kayalpattinam and nearby ports throng with pearl divers, merchants and ships, while Kulasekara sits in a stately Madurai hall listening to reports of prosperity.

dialogue.text: Marco Polo saw Ma'abar’s shore in these years—crowded quays, pearl divers, horse traders—and heard of five royal brothers sharing the Pandyan crown from Madurai.

i18n.hi: इन्हीं सालों में मार्को पोलो ने माबर का किनारा देखा—भीड़ भरे घाट, मोती खोजते गोताखोर, घोड़े बेचते सौदागर—और सुना कि मदुरै से पाँच भाई मिलकर पांड्य ताज संभाल रहे हैं।

panels.shot: medium court shot, Kulasekara flanked by unseen brothers (silhouettes/background)
panels.action: Kulasekara sits slightly forward on a carved throne, with the faint presence of other royal seats in the background, symbolizing brother-kings; courtiers present palm-leaf records and tribute.

dialogue.text: In inscriptions and chronicles, Maravarman Kulasekara emerges as the leading brother, ruling roughly from 1268 to 1308, bound to his siblings by blood and by power.

i18n.hi: शिलालेखों और क़िस्सों में मरवर्मन कुलसेकर मुखिया भाई बनकर उभरते हैं—लगभग 1268 से 1308 तक राज करते हुए, ख़ून और सत्ता दोनों से अपने भाइयों से बँधे हुए।

panels.shot: wide shot of coastal trade, slightly elevated viewpoint
panels.action: The camera overlooks dense rows of ships at anchor, Arab horse merchants bargaining, local traders measuring pearls, with Kulasekara observing from a balcony above the harbor.

dialogue.text: The Ma'abar coast fed their strength: foreign horses landed here, pearls gleamed in baskets, customs dues flowed to Madurai. Wealth linked them to the Indian Ocean world.

i18n.hi: माबर की तटरेखा ही उनकी ताकत का पेट थी—विदेशी घोड़े यहीं उतरते, टोकरी भर मोती चमकते, चुंगी का सोना मदुरै पहुँचता। यही दौलत उन्हें हिंदमहासागर की दुनिया से जोड़ती थी।

panels.shot: intimate court interior, Kulasekara in discussion with a learned advisor (advisor not in cast)
panels.action: Kulasekara leans over a map of the southern seas, arm pointing across the Palk Strait towards Sri Lanka, as an aged Brahmin advisor gestures gravely to distant lands.

dialogue.text: Across the narrow sea lay Sri Lanka, riven by rival kings. Pandyan influence occasionally touched the island; now, the chronicles say, Kulasekara turned his gaze there.

i18n.hi: सामने पतली सी खाड़ी के पार था श्रीलंका—टूटे फूटे, कई राजाओं में बँटा। कभी-कभी पांड्य असर वहाँ तक पहुँचता; अब, क़िस्से कहते हैं, कुलसेकर की नज़र उस टापू पर टिक गई।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle of Kulasekara boarding a ship
panels.action: At dawn, Kulasekara in armor steps onto a large wooden vessel, war banners fluttering, soldiers and sailors readying ropes as the fleet prepares to leave the Ma'abar coast.

dialogue.text: The Culavamsa, the Sri Lankan chronicle, tells of a Pandyan king named Kulasekara who gathered ships and men, and sailed to the island as an invader from the mainland.

i18n.hi: श्रीलंकाई ग्रंथ चूलवṁस कहता है कि कुलसेकर नाम का एक पांड्य राजा जहाज़ और सैनिक जुटाकर, ज़मीन पार से टापू पर चढ़ आया।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of Pandyan fleet on the sea
panels.action: A great flotilla of wooden warships cuts across deep blue water under heavy clouds, Kulasekara’s flagship at the center, its prow carved with a roaring tiger emblem.

dialogue.text: The Palk Strait lay between them and their goal. Wind filled their sails. Somewhere ahead stood Polonnaruwa and the most treasured object in Sri Lanka’s Buddhist world.

i18n.hi: उनके और उनके निशाने के बीच पड़ा पाल्क जलडमरूमध्य। हवा ने पाल भर दिए। आगे कहीं पोलोन्नरुवा था—और श्रीलंका की बौद्ध दुनिया की सबसे अनमोल धरोहर।

panels.shot: wide shot of Pandyan troops outside a Sri Lankan city
panels.action: Kulasekara stands before his assembled troops on Lankan soil, the walls and dagobas of a Sinhalese city visible in the distance, while smoke of siege fires rises.

dialogue.text: The Culavamsa speaks with anguish of Pandyan forces entering the island, of cities threatened and rulers challenged. Behind its words lies the shock of foreign arms at the heart of the island.

i18n.hi: चूलवṁस दर्द के साथ लिखता है—पांड्य सेनाएँ टापू में घुस आईं, नगरों पर खतरा, राजाओं को चुनौती। इन पंक्तियों के पीछे है बाहरी हथियारों का झटका, जो टापू के दिल तक आ पहुँचा।

panels.shot: solemn interior of a relic shrine, dramatic chiaroscuro
panels.action: Inside a dim shrine, monks kneel before a casket, while at the doorway Kulasekara and a few armored retainers appear, looking towards the sacred reliquary of the Buddha’s Tooth.

dialogue.text: At the center of the chronicle’s lament is one act: the Tooth Relic of the Buddha, kept in a jeweled casket, is said to have been seized by Kulasekara’s men and taken from the shrine.

i18n.hi: और इस मातम के बीच एक ही काम सबसे भारी है—रत्नों से जड़ी पेटी में रखा बुद्ध का दाँत-कुलसेकर के लोगों ने उसे मंदिर से उठा लिया और साथ ले गए।

panels.shot: close-up on Kulasekara holding the reliquary, face unreadable
panels.action: Kulasekara cradles a small ornate box, its surface inlaid with gems, his expression steady and reserved as dim temple light falls on his hands and the stunned faces of monks behind him.

dialogue.text: “This relic shall sail with us now,”

i18n.hi: “अब यह धरोहर हमारे साथ समुंदर चिरेगी।”

dialogue.text: For the Sinhalese authors, the Tooth was not a mere treasure. It embodied kingship and the Buddha’s presence. Its loss was recorded as a disaster for the island.

i18n.hi: सिंहल लेखकों के लिए यह दाँत साधारण ख़ज़ाना नहीं था—यही राजसत्ता का प्रतीक था, यही बुद्ध की मौजूदगी। इसका जाना टापू के लिए महाविपत्ति दर्ज हुआ।

panels.shot: wide shot of Pandyan fleet returning, shrine silhouette fading
panels.action: The Pandyan ships depart Sri Lanka under a grey sky, Kulasekara’s flagship leading; in the distance the outline of Lankan stupas diminishes as the fleet heads back toward Ma'abar.

dialogue.text: With the relic on board, the fleet turned back across the sea. The Culavamsa describes the Tooth Relic being carried away to the Pandyan land, leaving monks and kings to grieve.

i18n.hi: धरोहर जहाज़ पर चढ़ चुकी थी, तो बेड़ा वापस समुंदर पार मुड़ा। चूलवṁस बताता है कि बुद्ध का दाँत पांड्य-देश ले जाया गया, पीछे भिक्षु और राजा शोक में डूबे रह गए।

panels.shot: regal interior in Madurai, relic casket set apart
panels.action: Kulasekara sits in Madurai’s audience hall, the reliquary resting on a pedestal at a respectful distance, while envoys from Sri Lanka bow before him, hands folded in supplication.

dialogue.text: Yet the same chronicle also tells of negotiation. Lankan envoys petitioned the Pandyan court; letters and pleas crossed the sea, seeking the Tooth’s return from Kulasekara.

i18n.hi: पर इसी ग्रंथ में सुलह की बात भी है—लंका के दूत पांड्य दरबार पहुँचे; चिट्ठियाँ, गुहारें समुंदर पार गईं, कुलसेकर से दाँत लौटाने की माँग करती हुईं।

panels.shot: medium shot, Kulasekara in reflective pose by the casket
panels.action: Kulasekara stands alone near the reliquary in a quiet chamber, one hand resting on its side, eyes lowered in thought as lamplight flickers and throws long shadows.

dialogue.text: The Culavamsa presents a turning: after talks and agreements, Kulasekara ordered the relic to be sent back. The same king who took it chose to relinquish it.

i18n.hi: चूलवṁस आगे मोड़ दिखाता है—बातचीत और समझौते के बाद कुलसेकर ने धरोहर वापस भेजने का हुक्म दिया। जिसने लिया था, उसी राजा ने उसे छोड़ने का रास्ता चुना।

panels.shot: wide shot of a single ship bearing the relic towards Sri Lanka
panels.action: A solitary, dignified vessel sails over calm waters, a guarded reliquary visible on its deck; the coastline of Sri Lanka emerges faintly ahead in the mist.

dialogue.text: The chronicle describes the relic’s journey back, under Pandyan protection, to be restored to the island. For Sri Lanka’s Buddhists, it was a recovery of sanctity and legitimacy.

i18n.hi: ग्रंथ फिर उस वापसी-सफ़र का वर्णन करता है—पांड्य सुरक्षा में दाँत वापस टापू पहुँचा, फिर से स्थापित हुआ। श्रीलंका के बौद्धों के लिए यह पवित्रता और हक का लौटना था।

panels.shot: ceremonial interior in Sri Lanka, focus on monks and relic
panels.action: Sri Lankan monks and nobles gather in a great hall, bowing low as the reliquary is placed once more upon a high altar before a large Buddha image.

dialogue.text: The Culavamsa frames the episode from the island’s side: foreign seizure, deep distress, diplomacy, and finally rejoicing as the Tooth Relic was again enshrined in its home.

i18n.hi: चूलवṁस पूरा किस्सा टापू की नज़र से दिखाता है—विदेशी लूट, गहरी पीड़ा, राजनय, और अंत में खुशी जब बुद्ध का दाँत फिर अपने घर के गर्भगृह में लौट आया।

panels.shot: split-focus composition: Madurai wealth on one side, distant memory of Sri Lanka on the other
panels.action: Kulasekara sits in Madurai, with scenes of Ma'abar’s busy pearl markets and horse trade visible through open arches, while a faint vision of Lankan stupas appears beyond the horizon.

dialogue.text: In South Indian histories, Kulasekara stands among strong Pandyan rulers, enriching Madurai and its coasts. In Sri Lankan memory, he appears as the mainland king who once took, and then restored, their holiest relic.

i18n.hi: दक्षिण भारतीय तहरीरों में कुलसेकर मजबूत पांड्य राजाओं की कतार में खड़े हैं—मदुरै और उसके तटों को समृद्ध करते हुए। श्रीलंकाई याद में वे वही भू-राजा हैं, जिन्होंने कभी उनका पवित्रतम दाँत लिया, फिर उसे लौट भी दिया।

panels.shot: close-up on Kulasekara’s calm, weathered face, eyes looking past the viewer
panels.action: Kulasekara’s face fills the frame, lit softly, his gaze steady and distant, with an indistinct backdrop of sea and temple stone merging together.

dialogue.text: His age reminds us: power is measured not only by what it can seize from others, but also by what it chooses to give back when the world asks for its return.

i18n.hi: उनका दौर याद दिलाता है—ताकत केवल इससे नहीं तौली जाती कि वह क्या छीन सकती है, बल्कि इससे भी कि दुनिया जब वापस माँगे तो वह क्या लौटाने का साहस दिखाती है।

subtitle_i18n.en: The Five Brothers of Ma'abar and the Tooth of the Buddha
subtitle_i18n.hi: माबर के पाँच भाई और बुद्ध का दाँत
